description:
Problem: cloud builders (Claude Code on the web, Codex Cloud; docs/agent/cloud-builder.md) publish with make pr-open (cloud-builder.md:109). Once the local pre-PR review blocks pr-open until it can run, a session that cannot reach the gateway on the owner's Mac (127.0.0.1:4000) cannot open PRs. Owner decision 2026-10-25: give cloud builders gateway access over the tailnet with a cloud-scoped client token, rather than exempting them or stopping cloud publishing.

Outcome: a cloud session whose environment carries the cloud credentials joins the tailnet as tag:oracle-cloud and reaches only the gateway (https://<host>.<tailnet>.ts.net:4000, already served by tailscale serve; docs/internal/oracle-gateway-host.md:22) with a third gateway client, oracle-cloud, added through the mechanism of oracle-gateway-named-clients-20261025. make cloud-bootstrap starts tailscaled in userspace-networking mode with in-memory state when the credential is present, and exposes the tailnet to the review through a local proxy (SOCKS5 or HTTP) if userspace mode requires it. Without the credential, bootstrap still succeeds and reports that the gateway is unavailable. With it, bootstrap also installs the OMP build that CI's reviewers use (the pinned version and checksum in .github/workflows/oracle-verdict.yml) and verifies it, because the local review runs that harness; gate 1 also records the network allowlist entry its download needs.

Decision gates:
1. Feasibility, before owner setup: in a real Claude Code on the web session and a real Codex Cloud session, test whether tailscaled can run in userspace mode and reach controlplane.tailscale.com and a DERP relay under each platform's network settings, using a throwaway ephemeral key on a test tag the owner creates, or by documenting the exact network allowlist entries each platform needs. Record the result per platform. If a platform cannot reach the tailnet at all, stop and ask the owner (options: exempt that platform with a notice, or stop cloud publishing there).
2. Owner-only setup (settings and secrets): (a) tailnet policy: tagOwners for tag:oracle-cloud and one accept rule from tag:oracle-cloud to oracle-gateway:4000 only, mirroring tag:oracle-ci (oracle-gateway-host.md:43-54); (b) a Tailscale credential for cloud sessions: an ephemeral, pre-approved auth key tagged tag:oracle-cloud with an expiry, or an OAuth client limited to that tag; (c) cloud environment settings on each platform: ORACLE_GATEWAY_URL, the oracle-cloud token and the Tailscale credential, plus any network allowlist entries from gate 1. Write exact step-by-step instructions, block this item with that reason, ask the owner once, and resume when they confirm. The agent creates the oracle-cloud gateway client and its token file on the host.
3. Rotation: document how to rotate and revoke the oracle-cloud token and the Tailscale credential without touching oracle-ci or oracle-local.

Item guardrails: no change to tag:oracle-ci, the CI secrets, the oracle environment or the gateway bind; the cloud credential is ephemeral, tagged, and can reach only the gateway port; tokens never enter the repository, logs, PR bodies or tracker text; the agent edits no tailnet policy or cloud settings itself unless the owner supplies an API credential for that purpose in the current request; no paid cloud resources.

Common guardrails: work only in a linked worktree created by make worktree-create, then make agent-write-preflight; the primary clone is read-only. Never use git stash (refs/stash is shared across worktrees). Commit as Joe Harris <joeharris76@gmail.com>, staging explicit paths only; no git add -A, no --no-verify, no SKIP, no agent trailers. Durable text (commits, PR bodies, docs, comments) carries no tracker ids, session labels or plan references. Maintained code has no explanatory comments or docstrings (make comment-policy-check). Run make docs-reference-inventory-check and make doc-contracts-guard in addition to make pr-preflight. Close out with make pr-open, oracle SHIP on the exact head, make pr-arm; never raw gh pr merge, never a stand-in or bypass on these oracle soundness paths.
